From pages 29 and 30:

That is three times the Dutch national rate.

" Cannabis lifetime use in the Netherlands shows an expected increase, from 15.6 per cent in 1997 to 17 per cent in 2001. "

This is far below comparable figures for the UK and DEAland: UK (22.0% in 1996) and far lower than that of the US (32.9% in 1997.)

A major part of my forthcoming book, The Dutch Experience, will focus on the anti-Dutch prohibitionist propaganda waged by the international prohibitionist establishment.

In fact, one of the most fascinating aspects of cannabis prohibition is the development of prohibitionism as an international ideology. The purpose of ideology is to guide the " thinking " of adherents so that they will know how to react independently of any central direction. Thus one can find a similar party-line being followed around the world.

While one would expect that there would be an element of reefer madness about cannabis per se, it is interesting that anti-Dutch propaganda has become an integral part of the ideology.

Here are a series of items from around the world.

Indeed, this campaign often sinks to hatemongering, especially with the Swedish prohibitionists at the

Typically, the Swedish prohibitionists report on the new Dutch data under the header:

Within a two-day period in the last week in August, letters to the editors of papers in Canada and Florida were published with similar content. Nonetheless, I want to emphasize that I don't think that they were written from a template or from an organized letter-writing campaign, but rather they seem to be the result of ideology.

Taken individually they are not particularly important, and without the Internet we would never know about them, but the coincidence of their being published so far apart with similar content demonstrates an important point about the workings of ideologies generally and of prohibition in particular.

If letters are published simultaneously in different parts of the world that say that 2+2=4, that would hardly be noteworthy. However, when similar lies are told, something is going on.

Both of these letters refer to Amsterdam as though it and its Red Light District were typical of all of The Netherlands. That would be like saying that the Tenderloin in San Francisco is typical of California.

From Sarasota Florida Herald-Tribune
August 29, 2002
editor.letters@herald-trib.com
 http://www.newscoast.com/sarasota.cfm
By Frank P. Rock

LEAVE HOLLAND'S DOPE SCENE THERE

Kathleen Parker, in her column printed Aug. 20 in the Herald-Tribune ) ( " In drug war, honesty is best " ), advocates the legalization of marijuana. 

However, let's look at how this plan worked in real life in Holland. That country's experiment with legalization is now about 30 years old. If Ms. Parker walked the streets of Amsterdam she would observe a subculture of juvenile and adult potheads and addicts lying in alleys and doorways, day and night.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Juvenile and adult potheads and addicts lying in alleys and doorways, day and night "???

As noted, The Netherlands have a lower rate of cannabis and hard drug use than DEAland, so that would be hard to explain, if it were true...

Actually, I have to doubt that the writer has even been to Amsterdam.

Having just returned from there, and having walked through the seediest area of the Red Light district, I saw no one lying in doorways, which I see daily in Vancouver. I have also seen that sad scene in the London theater district. "

Amsterdam has become the drug supermarket of Europe. Every weekend people flock to Holland from all over Europe to stock up and then return home, where addiction is on the rise. The Dutch government is beginning to understand the social consequences of its " enlightened " drug policy, which seemed so promising 30 years ago. The country is now beginning to try to deal with these consequences by reinstituting tougher laws and controls
(MarijuanaNews note: This is a recurring part of the prohibitionist party line. But the fact is that the Dutch know that what they are doing is working much better than the alternative.

From The Saskatoon Saskatchewan StarPhoenix

POT ADVOCATES WILL NEVER LEARN LESSON

As I read the letter Police officer errs on several counts ( SP Aug. 21 ) from our old buddy Ken Sailor, I couldn't help but wonder why someone, with such an interest in poisoning himself, would continue to support such a cause.

Sailor always comes up with studies showing all the prejudice and misinformation about marijuana, and how well places such as Amsterdam have benefited from a more enlightened attitude...

Good for Amsterdam, if people there feel it has become a better place to live or to visit.

By the way, Amsterdam also allows euthanasia and legal exploitation of women (prostitution ). Sure doesn't sound like a great standard of living to me.
(MarijuanaNews note: Of course, that is a total non sequitur. Also it is ironic in that Nevada is the only state to have legal prostitution, and until last year it was the only state in which marijuana possession was a felony.)

Darcy Ecker
Saskatoon
